messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Parsing bug
parts:
In this chunk:


<<iacholxage-lsp,results=tex,h=5,w=7,cap='Linear spline surface for
males, with knots for age at 46, 52, 59 and knots for cholesterol at
196, 224, and 259 (quartiles).',scap='Linear spline surface for logit\\
{significant disease\\} for males'>>=
f <- lrm(sigdz ~ lsp(age,c(46,52,59)) *
(sex + lsp(cholesterol,c(196,224,259))),
data=acath)
latex(anova(f), caption='Linear spline surface',
file='', size='smaller')
bplot(Predict(f, cholesterol, age, np=40),
lfun=wireframe, zlim=zl, adj.subtitle=FALSE)
@

I get

Warning in parse_params(params) :
are you using old Sweave syntax? go http://yihui.name/knitr/options
Error: illegal tags in: iacholxage-lsp,results=tex,h=5,w=7,cap='Linear
spline surface for males, with knots for age at 46, 52, 59 and knots
for cholesterol at 196, 224, and 259 (quartiles).',scap='Linear spline
surface for logit\\{significant disease\\} for males'
all options must be of the form 'tag=value' except the chunk label
Execution halted


If I remove results=tex everything parses OK. I'm using the latest
version on github.

Thanks for any assistance,
Frank

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Parsing bug
parts:
should be results='tex', or better, results='asis'

knitr will issue errors or warnings whenever the new syntax fails, but
usually it does not matter, because it will just roll back to the old
way of paring options

To know the class of an option, see http://yihui.name/knitr/options
(e.g. results should be character)

However, in your case, the failure was a real failure, because when
knitr rolled back to the old syntax, it found commas in your words,
which should be escaped. Therefore neither the new nor the old syntax
could work for you.

Another problem is, you want to write \{ in TeX, which means you need
to write \\{ in R, which in turn means \\\\{ in the chunk option. This
is similar to how we write \ in regular expressions in R; please let
me know if you need more explanations.

Regards,
Yihui

appear in LaTeX you need \\{ \\} and not \\\\{ or \\\\}

Frank
